title: multi-nic-node-provision-debug-notes
content:
Context:
- Repro: new nodes provisioned in A/Z with 2 NICs (primary mgmt, secondary data) intermittently fail to join cluster or show NotReady for long periods. Affects kubelet/startup and CNI routes.
- Environment: Ubuntu 22.04 cloud image, cloud-init userdata, containerd 1.6.12, kubelet 1.27.x, kubeadm join workflow, calico v3.25.

Symptoms observed (notes):
- Node boots, cloud-init completes, but kubelet logs show repeated TLS bootstrap errors then pod sandbox failures.
- Sometimes node appears Ready for ~10-30s then goes NotReady.
- Intermittent failures only on instances with secondary NIC attached at boot; single-NIC VMs are stable.

Commands checked (raw):
- ip link show && ip addr show
- ethtool -k eth0; ethtool -k eth1
- journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p'
- sudo kubeadm join x.y.z:6443 --token <redacted> --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:<redacted> --v=5 2>&1 | tee /tmp/join.log
- sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init-output.log | tail -n 200
- cat /etc/netplan/50-cloud-init.yaml
- sudo grep -R "CNI" /var/log/* /var/log/containers/* || true

Observed log snippets (copied):
- kubelet: E0901 12:04:13.321004   12345 server.go:210] error creating certificate signing request: Post "https://x.y.z:6443/apis/certificates.k8s.io/v1/certificatesigningrequests": dial tcp x.y.z:6443: i/o timeout
- cloud-init: ds-identify: request to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ timed out
- containerd: time="2024-09-18T12:05:40Z" level=error msg="CreateContainer: failed to create containerd task: failed to create shim task: OCI runtime create failed: network not ready"
- calico/node: WARN FELIX: failed to allocate ipip tunnel route: "could not get route table for peer"

Hypotheses:
1) Secondary NIC is configured with DHCP and race condition causes default route flapping or metadata server no-route -> kubeadm/kubelet bootstrap can't reach control plane during early init.
2) cloud-init netplan ordering: netplan applied eth1 after eth0 so ephemeral DNS / route settings incorrect for a short window.
3) CNI plugin picks wrong interface for overlay traffic (Calico selecting non-mgmt interface without proper nat).
4) kube-proxy/iptables rules applied before host routes stable leading to pod networking failure and pod sandbox creation errors.
5) MTU mismatch on data NIC causing TCP seg/conn issues to api server in some AZs.

Commands and quick checks performed and result notes:
- curl -v --connect-timeout 2 http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/  -> sometimes times out, correlates with NotReady events.
- ip route show: sometimes two 0.0.0.0/0 via different devs; run 'ip route add default via <mgmt-gw> dev eth0 metric 50' to force primary route temporarily -> node joined reliably in that run.
- systemctl status systemd-networkd: OK, but cloud-init netplan apply logs show eth1 applied after eth0 in timing logs.
- sudo kubeadm join --v=5 log showed CSR post timeout at first; after forcing route to eth0 the CSR goes through and node becomes Ready.
- tcpdump -i eth1 icmp/arp: observed gratuitous ARP announcing same IP as another instance in rare cases (DHCP collision suspect).

Temporary mitigations tried:
- Add explicit default route in cloud-init post-boot (runcmd) to force mgmt via eth0. Helps but hacky.
- Set systemd-networkd link: /etc/systemd/network/10-eth0.link to set MAC order hint -> reduced occurrences but not gone.
- Disabled auto-configure of eth1 by cloud-init (set network: {config: disabled} for secondary) -> stable but customer concerned about manual config requirement.

Longer-term fixes to evaluate:
- Ensure cloud-init netplan includes explicit routing table and metric for mgmt NIC; use renderer: networkd, set optional: true on data NIC to prevent blocking.
- Update provisioning template to attach secondary NIC after guest-init completes (post-boot attach via provider API) to avoid early route flaps.
- Add pre-kubelet systemd unit that verifies metadata server reachable (curl) and that default route is via eth0 before starting kubelet.
- Change CNI config to force host interface selection (calico.ipip enabled + IP_AUTODETECTION_METHOD to interface=eth0 or CIDR-based detection) so overlay uses mgmt iface until data is ready.
- Add an init container in node-problem-detector that checks for dual-default-route and marks node unschedulable until fixed? (discussion needed)

Repro steps to validate changes (proposal):
1) Build test image with cloud-init change (disable DHCP on eth1) and boot 10 nodes in staging with same AZ mix.
2) Boot another 10 nodes with post-attach secondary NIC via provider API at t+120s.
3) Monitor kubelet/join times, cloud-init metadata reachability, and calico logs. Use k9s + `kubectl get nodes -w -o wide` to watch readiness.
4) Run iperf multihop between pods to validate MTU.

Useful commands to capture next run (copy-pastable):
- journalctl -u cloud-init -b -o cat > /tmp/cloudinit.log
- journalctl -u kubelet -b -o short-precise > /tmp/kubelet.log
- sudo ip -4 route show table main > /tmp/route-main.txt
- sudo netplan get > /tmp/netplan.yaml
- sudo tcpdump -nne -i any host 169.254.169.254 -w /tmp/metadata.pcap & sleep 40; pkill -f tcpdump
- sudo crictl ps -a; sudo crictl logs <podsandbox-id>

Open questions / next actions for triage:
- Is there a cloud-provider kernel bug causing duplicate ARP? Need cloud provider network team to confirm (raise ticket).
- If we force ip detection for calico to eth0, will we break multi-homed pod traffic expectations? Validate with multi-NIC pod scenarios.
- Should kubelet be gated on metadata server reachability or on route stability? Tradeoff: faster boot vs. correctness.

Notes to self / quick TODOs:
- OCR the cloud-init YAMLs from instances that failed and succeeded; diff them (done: attach in linked_artifacts).
- Add small systemd health-check unit to repo that pings metadata server and exits 0 only when route is correct (PR: infra/provisioning#TODO).
- Schedule sync with cloud-networking team (Marco + cloud infra) to look at DHCP lease collisions window.

Last quick timestamped trial (2024-09-24 14:33):
- Provisioned 3 nodes with eth1 disabled via cloud-init -> all Joined and Ready within 45s.
- Re-provisioned 3 nodes with eth1 active at boot -> 2/3 had initial CSR timeout and required manual route fix; tcpdump showed metadata server unreachable for 20-40s during boot window.

Appendix: snippets of helpful docs/flags
- Calico autodetection: IP_AUTODETECTION_METHOD: interface=^eth0$ or can use can-reach=8.8.8.8
- kubelet startup flags to consider: --node-status-update-frequency, --register-with-taints for temp isolation
- netplan reference: https://netplan.io/reference

If I forget: prioritization right now = 1) short-term cloud-init default-route fix (low risk), 2) calico ip autodetect change (medium risk, test), 3) provider-level attach-after-init (higher operational cost but clean).

End of scratchpad.
